questions.prompt: A model has a 1,000-token window. Your request is about 700 tokens. What is the longest answer it can write?
options: 1,000 tokens, because the answer has its own window
1,700 tokens, the input plus a full window
700 tokens, the same size as the input
About 300 tokens, because input and answer share the window
questions.explanation: Input and output share one window. 1,000 minus 700 leaves about 300 tokens for the reply; past that, the answer is cut off.

questions.prompt: You send a 4,200-character request to a model with a 1,000-token window. What happens?
options: The model reads the first 1,000 tokens and ignores the rest
The provider rejects the request, because about 1,050 tokens is more than the whole window
The model replies with an empty answer but accepts the request
The window grows to fit the request
questions.explanation: At about 4 characters per token, 4,200 characters is about 1,050 tokens, 50 more than the window. A request that does not fit is refused as a whole.

questions.prompt: Your program read a file earlier, but that text was not included in this request. What does the model know about the file?
options: Nothing, because the model only sees what is inside this request
Everything, because it stores files it has seen
questions.explanation: The window is the model's whole working space for one request. A fact outside it does not exist for the model.
